pulls.body:
## Summary

- Mask config keys containing `ct0` in `Config.to_dict()` so `twitter_ct0` is no longer returned in plaintext.
- Add a regression test that verifies `twitter_ct0` follows the same masked output path as other credential keys.
- Clean up pre-existing lint noise in the touched config test file.

## Root Cause

`Config.to_dict()` only treated keys containing `key`, `token`, `password`, or `proxy` as sensitive. The Twitter/X CSRF token key is named `twitter_ct0`, so it missed that substring check and could be exposed by diagnostic output.

Fixes #412.

- `uv run pytest tests/test_config.py -q`
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`
- `uv run ruff check agent_reach/config.py tests/test_config.py`

pulls.title: feat(providers): OCC Mundial — Mexico's dominant job board
pulls.body:
## What

Adds a zero-auth scanner provider for **[occ.com.mx](https://www.occ.com.mx)** (OCC Mundial), the dominant general job board in Mexico, plus 18 offline tests.

Per CONTRIBUTING, new zero-auth scanner providers go straight to a PR without an issue first. Happy to open one if you'd rather discuss direction.

## Why

A large share of Mexican employers never appear on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday or SuccessFactors. Mid-size industrials and domestic groups post to OCC instead, so the scanner has a structural hole in Mexico that no amount of ATS probing closes.

I hit this concretely: I resolved 30+ ATS tenants by hand (Workday, SuccessFactors, SmartRecruiters) to widen Mexico coverage, and the Mexican mid-market still did not show up. Checking a few directly — Xignux, Deacero — they publish on OCC, not on any international ATS.

A live scan across 8 keywords × 6 states returned **1,136 postings, 95 of which survived `title_filter`, from 69 companies no ATS sweep had ever returned**. A sample:

| Company | Role | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Tecnoap | Ingeniero en Automatización | San Nicolás de los Garza, NL |
| AWL Automation | Service PLC Engineer | Colón, Querétaro |
| IMVISION | Ingeniero de Aplicaciones — Visión Artificial | Querétaro |
| SSS CARRIER | Técnico de mantenimiento PLC (Allen Bradley) | Santa Catarina, NL |
| Kimberly Clark de México | Ing. procesos Mecatrónico/Robótico | Cuautitlán Izcalli |

## How

There is no public JSON API — `/api/*` answers `403`. The search pages are server-rendered, so the provider parses the job cards out of the markup with the same tiny-tag-extractor approach already used by `weworkremotely.mjs` and `successfactors.mjs`. **No new dependencies.**

Config shape:

```yaml
  - name: OCC Mundial
    provider: occ
    queries: [automatizacion, robotica, mecatronica]
    states: [nuevo-leon, jalisco]   # optional; omit for nationwide
    max_pages: 3                    # optional, default 3, hard cap 10
```

## Two behaviours worth flagging

**1. Pagination is a slug suffix, not a query parameter.** `?page=2`, `?pagina=2`, `?p=2`, `?start=20`, `?offset=20` and `/2/` all return `HTTP 200` with a full page of cards — from page 1. The failure is completely silent, so a naive implementation re-reads page 1 forever and looks like it is working. The only shape that advances is:

```
https://www.occ.com.mx/empleos/de-{keyword}-pagina-{N}/
```

Because OCC also answers an out-of-range page with page 1 rather than an empty result, the fetch loop additionally stops as soon as a page yields no new ids. Both are covered by tests.

**2. `"Empresa confidencial"` is OCC's own placeholder, not an employer name.** It is normalized to the locale-invariant `?` marker (#1596) so the Spanish string never reaches the tracker or a report.

## Tests

`tests/providers/occ.test.mjs` — 18 assertions, **all offline** against a fixture of the real card markup, so CI never depends on occ.com.mx being reachable.

Covers: provider shape · page-1 URL has no suffix · pagination uses the `-pagina-N` slug · accent folding and the `en-{state}` segment · URLs cannot be steered off the `occ.com.mx` origin · entity decoding in title and location · posting URL built from `data-id` · malformed cards dropped · `"Empresa confidencial"` → `?` · empty input → `[]` · dedup when page 1 is re-served · loop stops on no new ids · normalized output shape · transport errors do not kill the board · `max_pages` capped at 10.

```
$ node test-all.mjs --only providers/occ
📊 Results: 18 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings
```

## Follow-up, not in this PR

Computrabajo is the other portal with the same footprint in Mexico. Same argument, separate provider — happy to do it if this shape looks right to you.

pulls.title: fix(providers): radancy stops trusting totalResults, cache-busts JSON, retries every fetch
pulls.body:
## Summary

Live-audited every Radancy (TalentBrew) tenant reachable from this session's `portals.yml` entry plus several found via web search, and found three independent, unrelated problems behind `radancy.mjs`'s `⚠️ truncated ... raise max_jobs/max_pages` warning: one tenant loses real postings to a caching bug, several tenants have a `totalResults` banner that simply overstates what their own search index serves on both transports, and one very large tenant hits a hard pagination-window ceiling at its backend. None of the three is fixed by raising `max_pages`/`max_jobs`, which is exactly the advice the current warning gives every time.

## Problem 1 — a caching bug drops and duplicates postings on Munich Re Group

Walking `careers.munichre.com`'s JSON fragment endpoint end-to-end and recording every `(page, id, title, location, url)` tuple showed the same posting reappearing on a second, distant page with byte-identical content, while a different posting never appeared on any page at all. Reproduced on 9 consecutive full walks with the same pages and the same magnitude every time (not random drift): 5 duplicated ids, always on the same page pairs.

Isolated the cause by testing two independent changes against the same tenant: `Cache-Control: no-cache` + `Pragma: no-cache` request headers made no difference (9/9 runs still broken), but a random per-request query parameter — forcing a cache-key miss — made it 0/9 broken. Re-running the same walk through the `?p=N` HTML transport (the same underlying data, a different route) never showed the problem at all, which further narrows it to a caching layer in front of the JSON route specifically, not the tenant's own data.

## Problem 2 — `totalResults` overstates reality on several tenants, and that's normal for this platform

Separately, four of nine fully-audited tenants (from a small board to Radancy's own corporate careers site) collected 10-56% fewer unique postings than their `data-total-results` banner claims, with zero duplicate rows anywhere. Re-walking two of them through the `?p=N` HTML transport reproduced the identical shortfall to the exact posting count, proving it isn't a transport bug — the tenant's own search index simply doesn't contain as many retrievable postings as its own counter claims. Cache-busting (the Problem 1 fix) made no difference to this shortfall on any of the affected tenants, confirming it's a separate issue.

`data-total-pages`, unlike `data-total-results`, matched the walk's own natural end (a short or empty final page) in every one of the 9 tenants checked, so it stays a valid bound for the walk itself — only the results counter is untrustworthy.

## Problem 3 — Walgreens hits a hard pagination-window ceiling at exactly 10,000

Walgreens (22,813 claimed postings, the largest tenant checked) was excluded from the count above and audited separately: a full 229-page walk shows pages 1-100 each returning a full 100 rows (10,000 total, no duplicates anywhere), then every page from 101 through 229 returning a clean, structured "no jobs" response (`hasJobs: false`, an empty results fragment) rather than an error or a short page. The cutoff lands exactly at offset 10,000 — 100 pages of 100 — the textbook default `max_result_window` ceiling on an Elasticsearch/Solr-style backend (one tenant observed so far, not established across the platform the way `workday.mjs`'s analogous `WORKDAY_OFFSET_CEILING` is). This isn't a caching artifact (a 130-page gap of identical empty responses isn't a stale cache hit) and it isn't recoverable by pagination cleverness on our side, unlike workday's clamp: TalentBrew's JSON fragment API exposes no documented facet-style split to route around it, so the backend simply refuses to serve past that offset no matter how the walk asks.

This surfaced a real gap while testing the fix live: with the *default* `max_jobs` (2,000), the walk correctly stops there first — page 20, well before the backend's own 10,000 ceiling — and now correctly warns (`truncated at 2,000 of 22,813 jobs`, `stopReason: 'cap'`), because raising `max_jobs` genuinely would recover more, up to 10,000. Only past that point does the *other* behavior apply: with `max_jobs` raised above 10,000, the walk runs to the backend's own empty page at 101 and returns exactly 10,000 with no warning, because past there raising anything no longer helps. Verified both live.

## The fix

- `buildFragmentUrl()` now appends a random `_` query parameter to every JSON fragment request, unique per call. Verified against all 11 live tenants seen in this investigation (including the one that already fails for an unrelated reason) that this changes nothing for a tenant that didn't have the caching problem — page-1 output matched with and without it in every case.
- The walk now tracks *why* it stopped (`stopReason`, matching the `workday.mjs`/`phenom.mjs` convention already used elsewhere in this file) instead of comparing the accumulated count against `totalResults`. The `raise max_jobs/max_pages` warning now fires only when `max_pages`/`max_jobs` demonstrably cut the walk short of the source's own larger page count — never when the walk ran to the source's own natural end and merely fell short of an inflated results counter, and never on a mid-walk fetch error (which now gets its own distinct, immediate log line instead of failing silently).
- `resolveMaxJobs()` now clamps a user-supplied `max_jobs` the same way `resolveMaxPages()` already clamps `max_pages` — noticed while testing Walgreens live: `max_pages` was already defended against a garbage config value, `max_jobs` wasn't. Not a resource-safety fix (the page loop was always independently bounded by `max_pages`, so an unclamped `max_jobs` never risked an unbounded walk) — just closing a defensive-coding gap between the two, capped at the true ceiling the JSON transport can ever return (`MAX_PAGES * FRAGMENT_RECORDS_PER_PAGE`).

environment: Codewhale 审批引擎及工具执行路径

pulls.title: feat(claude): disclose AI authorship in posts and share credential-read denials
pulls.body:
Two pieces of a personal AI-usage policy get support here: posts written with AI say so, and the agent's file tools cannot read secrets on any machine these dotfiles set up.

## Disclosure

`.claude/INSTRUCTIONS.md` gains one sub-bullet under the external-write rule: a comment, reply or message others will read says it was written with AI, unless the destination's own convention says otherwise.
Claude Code attributes only commits and pull request bodies, so review replies and messages posted under the user's account carried no disclosure before.
A fresh reader under the new line added the disclosure to review comments it drafted for the user to paste, and posted text the user dictated unchanged.

## Shared read denials

- `.claude/settings.base.json` holds permission rules every machine shares. It denies reads of names that are plainly secret (`.env` and its local variants, private keys, `credentials.json`, `client_secret*.json`, `.netrc`, Terraform state) and of credential directories (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, gcloud, …), following the list rtk-ai/rtk#2827 curates. It asks before names that may or may not hold a secret (`*.pem`, `.npmrc`, `*.tfvars`). `.env.example`, `.env.sample` and `.env.template` stay readable through `!` carve-outs.
- `mise run setup:claude-settings` merges the base into the machine's own `~/.claude/settings.json`, which stays machine-local because `rtk init` and the `/config` panel write into it. Each array gets the base's entries first in base order and keeps the machine's own after them, so a rerun changes nothing, a sorted list gets the carve-outs back behind `Read(.env.*)`, and a machine can add its own denials or carve-outs.
- The README says what the rules do not do: they are not exhaustive, and on a machine running the rtk hook, `cat`, `head`, `tail` and `grep` are rewritten to `rtk read` and `rtk grep`, which the Read rules do not reach (rtk-ai/rtk#2428, closed without a fix). That gap is left to upstream rather than traded against rtk's savings.

The rules were checked by running `claude -p` against dummy files: each secret name was refused, the ambiguous ones raised a permission request, and templates, public keys and ordinary files were read. The merge script was run against missing, empty, sorted and hand-edited settings files, and fails on invalid JSON rather than overwriting it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Merge the tracked .claude/settings.base.json into the machine's ~/.claude/settings.json.
+# The machine file keeps whatever else it holds (hooks `rtk init` patched in, keys the
+# /config panel wrote), which is why the base is merged rather than symlinked.
+# Objects merge key by key; an array starts with the base's entries in the base's order
+# and keeps the machine's own after them, so a `!` carve-out, the base's or the
+# machine's, still follows the rules it carves from after the machine file was sorted;
+# any other base value replaces the machine's. A rerun changes nothing.
+# Removing an entry from the base does not remove it here; edit the machine file for that.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+script_dir=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+base="$script_dir/../.claude/settings.base.json"
+target="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
+
+# An empty file reads as {} so it is filled rather than reported as already merged.
+current='{}'
+[ -f "$target" ] && current=$(jq -s 'add // {}' "$target")
+
+merged=$(jq --argjson base "$(cat "$base")" '
+  def merge($b):
+    if type == "object" and ($b | type) == "object" then
+      reduce ($b | keys_unsorted[]) as $k (.; .[$k] |= merge($b[$k]))
+    elif type == "array" and ($b | type) == "array" then
+      $b + (. - $b)
+    else
+      $b
+    end;
+  merge($base)
+' <<<"$current")
+
+if [ "$merged" = "$(jq . <<<"$current")" ]; then
+  echo "$target already holds everything in the base"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+diff -u <(jq . <<<"$current") <(echo "$merged") || true
+tmp=$(mktemp "$target.XXXXXX")
+echo "$merged" >"$tmp"
+mv "$tmp" "$target"
+echo "updated $target"

pulls.title: fix(cmds): block .env reads in native content subcommands (#2428)
pulls.body:
Closes #2428. **Stacked on #2354** — please review/merge that first. Until #2354 lands, the diff here also includes its proxy commit; the native-reader change is the top commit (`781546d`).

## Problem
Companion to #2345 (which fixed `rtk proxy`). rtk's own content-reading subcommands read `.env` with no gate:

```
$ printf 'PASSWORD=hunter2\n' > .env
$ rtk read .env
PASSWORD=hunter2        # verbatim dump, exit 0
```

So a `.env` deny is bypassed via `rtk read` / `grep` / `diff` / `log` / `smart` — the same credential-exfiltration class as CVE-2026-33068, via rtk itself rather than proxy.

## Fix
Reuse the proxy `.env` guard through a shared `permissions::env_read_refusal` helper and refuse a `.env` file-path argument (before the file is opened) in the `read` / `grep` / `diff` / `log` / `smart` arms. Same semantics as proxy: `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` are allowed.

- The grep search **pattern** is intentionally not inspected (only the path + file args), so `rtk grep .env Makefile` still works.
- Directory listers (`ls` / `tree` / `find`) are name-only and left **unchanged**: rtk intentionally shows `.env` in listings (`src/cmds/system/constants.rs`). Name disclosure is out of scope here.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean (`warnings = "deny"`)
- `cargo test --all`: 2164 passed, 0 failed (2 new helper tests)
- End-to-end against a live `.env`: `rtk read/grep/diff/log/smart .env` are refused (exit 1) and the secret leaks **0 times**; `rtk read plain.txt` and `rtk read .env.example` still work.

pulls.title: fix(fetch_url): add allow_private_ip_hosts to skip DNS-resolved IP check
pulls.body:
## Problem

`fetch_url` unconditionally rejects requests when a hostname resolves to a private/reserved IP address. This breaks users whose DNS is managed by a transparent proxy that returns virtual private-range addresses for all external domains — every outbound request fails with `resolved IP x.x.x.x is a restricted address`, and there is no way to override it. Fixes #1071.

## Solution

Add `allow_private_ip_hosts = false` to the `[network]` config table. When set to `true`, the SSRF guard skips the check on **DNS-resolved** IPs, allowing the request to proceed through the proxy. Literal private-IP addresses typed directly into a URL (e.g. `http://10.0.0.1/admin`) are **always** blocked regardless of this setting, preserving the core SSRF protection.

The error message when a resolved IP is rejected now mentions the new option so users know how to unblock their setup.

## Changes

- `crates/tui/src/network_policy.rs` — add `allow_private_ip_hosts: bool` field to `NetworkPolicy`; expose `allows_private_ip_hosts()` on `NetworkPolicyDecider`
- `crates/tui/src/config.rs` — add `allow_private_ip_hosts` to `NetworkPolicyToml` and propagate through `into_runtime()`
- `crates/tui/src/tools/fetch_url.rs` — consult the flag before rejecting DNS-resolved private IPs; improve error message
- `config.example.toml` — document the new option
- `crates/tui/src/tools/web_run.rs`, `crates/tui/tests/skill_install.rs` — fill new field in existing `NetworkPolicy` literals

## Testing

All existing tests pass (`cargo test --package deepseek-tui`).
